searchText: Devnet 12 seems to struggle right now, we are looking into it lodestar nethermind looks fine lodestar-reth seems to struggle. reth doesn't seem to be responding it seems like all reth nodes are struggling actually I spammed today with a few thousands of 6-blob txs and a few thousands of 1-blob txs - was trying to check if nethermind blob pool is correctly keeping capacity. Finished spamming about 1h ago. Seems like devnet-12 problems may be triggered by my action, not sure why <@&1070471163219824730> and <@&595681804422479873> are the ones reporting major issues there are some nimbus clients producing orphaned blocks ( nimbus-nethermind-1-arm, nimbus-besu-1, nimbus-geth-1), each of them basically has their own chain. the clients where reporting `Block quarantine full (blobless)` for some time and are forked off since then Besu in prysm-besu-1 & prysm-besu-1-arm is having problems building blocks since an hour ago. There are some stack traces in the logs. Can someone from <@&836981603216654336> have a look? only the prysm pairs seem affected, but the errors look bad <@412614104222531604> I think more clients than Nimbus and Reth have issues I think some of it was caused by OOM 8gb ram is just really not cutting it anymore for devnet 12 question if: this is not limited and clients would OOM with 16GB as well geth is returning `beacon syncer reorging` on fcu calls, not sure what it means or if it is possible to optimize or limit blob tx pool to be able to test on 8GB geth seems to run oom as well cc <@363800010518822915> : ``` time="2024-02-01 14:44:07" level=debug msg="BlobSidecar not found in db, root=c078477fa702ddb0840a95f84f8d6365049520131455ccb2165063b1f0b0c634, index=2" error="open /data/blobs/0xc078477fa702ddb0840a95f84f8d6365049520131455ccb2165063b1f0b0c634/2.ssz: no such file or directory" handler="blob_sidecars_by_root" prefix=sync ``` can we safely ignore this? will it just fetch from network the next chance it gets? Yeah, we can ignore that. That means a node is requesting a sidecar from us that we dont have. It could be a lazy node that's requesting "everything" or prysm just sync'ed to head and doesnt have anything yet clients defaults should be set up for memory budgets
